title: Follicular lymphoma
subtitle: The prototype indolent lymphoma — incurable when advanced, but usually a disease measured in many years. Treat symptoms and burden (GELF), not the scan; POD24 and transformation are the events that change prognosis. Old grade 3B is now follicular large B-cell lymphoma — treat as DLBCL
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin — follicular lymphoma · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Biology and classification
rows: BCL2 juxtaposed to the IGH enhancer → BCL2 overexpression blocks apoptosis. Germinal-center phenotype: CD20+, CD10+, BCL6+, BCL2+; CD5−, CD23− (usually). CREBBP / KMT2D / EZH2 mutations are common secondary hits
Old grades 1, 2 and 3A. Grading is now optional — poorly reproducible and of little value for individual treatment. Grade 3A is managed as FL
WHO-HAEM5 name for old grade 3B (sheets of centroblasts, no centrocytes; often CD10− and t(14;18)−). Treat as DLBCL with R-CHOP. ICC 2022 keeps the name “FL grade 3B”
Variants that should not be over-treated
Pediatric-type FL (young, localized, BCL2−, excellent outcome) · duodenal-type FL (low dissemination risk) · in situ follicular B-cell neoplasm (incidental)

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Excisional or generous core biopsy — architecture and centroblast content cannot be judged on FNA
PET/CT for staging; Lugano / Ann Arbor. Marrow biopsy when it would change management (e.g. apparent limited stage before RT)
CBC, CMP, LDH, β2-microglobulin, HBsAg + anti-HBc (reactivation with anti-CD20), HCV, HIV
Biopsy the PET-hottest lesion if SUV is discordant or one node grows out of step — it is the site most likely to have transformed

blocks.heading: FLIPI — “NoLASH”, 1 point each
blocks.footnote: Nodal areas >4 · LDH >ULN · Age ≥60 · Stage III–IV · Hgb <12 (Solal-Céligny, Blood 2004; pre-rituximab era). FLIPI-2: age >60, β2M >ULN, marrow involved, Hgb <12, largest node >6 cm — 5-yr PFS 80% / 51% / 19%. Neither index tells you when to treat — GELF does.

boxes: 4 Gy ×2 is inferior for durable control (FoRT)
adding R-CVP to RT improved PFS, not OS (TROG 99.03)
PFS gain, no OS gain — weigh infections

blocks.heading: GELF — any one = high burden, treat
rows: Any nodal or extranodal mass ≥7 cm
B symptoms or other disease-related symptoms
Splenomegaly · effusion or ascites · organ compression
blocks.footnote: Brice, JCO 1997. Meeting none = observe. Watch-and-wait has never lost survival against early treatment; rituximab ×4 delays the need for next therapy (3-yr no new treatment 88% vs 46%, HR 0.21; Ardeshna, Lancet Oncol 2014) but has not improved OS.

blocks.heading: First-line evidence
rows: BR: median PFS 69.5 vs 31.2 mo, HR 0.58, far less toxicity (no alopecia, less neuropathy). No OS difference

7-yr PFS 63.4% vs 55.7%; OS identical (88.5% vs 87.2%). More serious AEs (48.9% vs 43.4%) and infusion reactions. With bendamustine: more grade 3–5 infections, second cancers and fatal events — prolonged T-cell depletion
Negative superiority trial — 6-yr PFS 60% vs 59%, OS 89% both. An equivalent chemo-free option: less neutropenia, more rash
Median PFS 10.5 vs 4.1 yr at 9 yr follow-up; no OS benefit; grade 2–4 infections 39% vs 24%
Rituximab retreatment at progression = maintenance for time to treatment failure (3.9 vs 4.3 yr), using 4 vs 18 doses

blocks.html: POD24 is the prognostic event that matters. ~20% progress within 2 years of first-line chemoimmunotherapy; their 5-yr OS is ~50% vs ~90% (FLIPI-adjusted HR 6.4; Casulo, JCO 2015). Implications: rebiopsy (a large share are transformed), avoid simply repeating the same chemo, and move early to R²-based triplets, CAR-T or bispecifics; consolidate chemosensitive relapse with auto-HCT in selected patients.

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: FLIPI prognosticates; GELF decides. A high FLIPI with no GELF criterion is still a reason to observe
No first-line upgrade has improved survival — not obinutuzumab, not maintenance, not R². Choose on toxicity and patient priorities
Old grade 3B (FLBL) gets R-CHOP, not BR; grade 3A is treated as FL
Rebiopsy every progression that looks different — POD24, a discordant node, a hot PET lesion, a rising LDH
Think ahead to CAR-T before giving bendamustine to a high-risk patient

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — relapsed disease, withdrawn agents, transformation, dosing and toxicity

blocks.heading: Relapsed / refractory — the agents
rows: AUGMENT (phase 3, FL + MZL, not rituximab-refractory): PFS 39.4 vs 14.1 mo, HR 0.46; 5-yr update OS HR 0.59. Benefit carried by FL — the MZL subgroup was not significant
EPCORE FL-1 (phase 3, ≥1 prior line): ORR 95% vs 79%, PFS HR 0.21, 16-mo PFS 85.5% vs 40.2%. Grade ≥3 AEs 90% vs 68%; CRS low grade (gr 2 in 5%). OS immature
inMIND (phase 3, double-blind): median PFS 22.4 vs 13.9 mo, HR 0.43. No CRS — a fit for patients unsuited to T-cell engagers
Single-arm phase 2, 3L+: CR 60%; fixed duration — 8 cycles if CR, up to 17. CRS 44%, mostly grade 1–2. CELESTIMO (+ lenalidomide vs R², 2L+) met PFS — topline only, Sept 2026
EPCORE NHL-1 FL cohort, 3L+: ORR 82%, CR 62.5%; continuous until progression. 3-step-up dosing cut CRS to 49% (none ≥grade 3)
ZUMA-5 (single arm, 3L+): ORR 94% FL; median PFS 62.2 mo (all iNHL) at 5-yr follow-up; few relapses after 30 mo. Grade ≥3 neurotoxicity 19%
TRANSCEND FL: 3L+ ORR 97%, CR 94%; 2L high-risk (POD24) ORR 96%. CRS 58% (grade ≥3 1%)
ROSEWOOD (randomized phase 2 vs obinutuzumab): ORR 69% vs 46%, median PFS 28.0 vs 10.4 mo. Confirmatory MAHOGANY (vs R²) ongoing
blocks.footnote: No head-to-head data between CAR-T and bispecifics. CAR-T gives the most durable single-shot responses; bispecifics are off-the-shelf and outpatient. Recent bendamustine blunts CAR-T expansion and outcome (ZUMA-5) — plan the sequence.

blocks.heading: Withdrawn — do not reach for these
rows: Accelerated approval 2020 (3L+ EZH2-mutant, or no alternative). Withdrawn from the US market 2026: in SYMPHONY-1 (+ R²), hematologic second cancers (MDS/AML, B-ALL) in 5.7% vs 0%, 3 deaths

Idelalisib, duvelisib FL indications withdrawn 2021–22; umbralisib withdrawn 2022 (excess deaths); copanlisib withdrawn Nov 2023 (CHRONOS-4 negative). Class problem: infections, colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, and an OS signal
Never approved for FL; confirmatory SELENE (FL/MZL) missed PFS

blocks.heading: Transformation
items: 10-yr cumulative risk ~5–8% in the rituximab era (5.2% with rituximab vs 8.7% without; Aristotle, Lancet Haematol 2018)
Suspect it with discordant nodal growth, new B symptoms, rising LDH, hypercalcemia, new extranodal disease, or a PET lesion much hotter than the rest
Biopsy the PET-hottest site — a random node can miss it. Check MYC: with the existing BCL2 rearrangement a MYC break makes it HGBL with MYC + BCL2
Treat as DLBCL: anthracycline-naïve → R-CHOP; already had R-CHOP → salvage + auto-HCT or CAR-T (axi-cel, liso-cel and tisa-cel labels include DLBCL arising from FL)

blocks.heading: How to choose at relapse
items: Late relapse, low burden: rituximab again, or R². Symptomatic, first relapse: epcoritamab + R² is now the strongest randomized 2L data; tafasitamab + R² if a T-cell engager is not suitable
POD24 or double-refractory (anti-CD20 + alkylator): favor CAR-T (liso-cel has 2L POD24 data) or a bispecific; auto-HCT for chemosensitive early relapse
Frail: rituximab alone, R², or zanubrutinib + obinutuzumab. Palliation of a symptomatic node: 2 × 2 Gy

blocks.heading: Regimen dosing
rows: 375 mg/m² weekly ×4; maintenance 375 q8 wk ×2 yr (PRIMA). SC rituximab 1400 mg after a first full IV dose
Rituximab 375, cyclophosphamide 750, vincristine 1.4 (max 2 mg) d1, prednisone 40 mg/m² d1–5, ± doxorubicin 50 — q21d ×6 (CHOP) or ×8 (CVP)
1000 mg flat, C1 d1, 8, 15, then d1 of each cycle (C2–6 with benda, C2–8 with CHOP/CVP); maintenance 1000 mg q2 mo ×2 yr
Lenalidomide 20 mg PO d1–21 q28d ×12 (10 mg if CrCl 30–59); rituximab 375 weekly C1 then d1 C2–5
Epcoritamab 48 mg SC after step-up, weekly C1–3, then q4wk C4–12 (fixed duration) + R² as above
SC 0.16 → 0.8 → 3 → 48 mg (C1 d1, 8, 15, 22), 48 mg weekly C2–3, q2wk C4–9, then q4wk until progression
IV 1 → 2 → 60 mg (C1 d1, 8, 15), 60 mg C2 d1, then 30 mg q21d; stop after 8 cycles if CR, else up to 17
Tafasitamab 12 mg/kg d1, 8, 15, 22 C1–3, then d1+15 C4–12 (q28d) + R²
Zanubrutinib 160 mg BID continuous + obinutuzumab 1000 mg (C1 d1, 8, 15; C2–6 d1; then q8wk)
24 Gy / 12 fx curative intent · 2 × 2 Gy palliative
blocks.footnote: mg/m² unless stated. Premedicate every anti-CD20 infusion (acetaminophen, antihistamine, steroid for the first).

blocks.heading: Toxicity and monitoring
items: HBV: screen HBsAg + anti-HBc before any anti-CD20; entecavir prophylaxis if either positive, continued for ≥12 months after the last dose

Bendamustine → profound, prolonged CD4 lymphopenia (months to years). Give PJP prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) and VZV prophylaxis (acyclovir/valacyclovir); watch for CMV. Worse when followed by maintenance anti-CD20 — think twice about stacking them. Also hampers later CAR-T manufacturing
Obinutuzumab: infusion reactions ~60% (mostly C1 d1) — premedicate, slow first infusion, hold antihypertensives. More neutropenia and infection than rituximab

Bispecifics: CRS clusters around the first full dose of step-up. Corticosteroid premedication, hydration, close monitoring after the first full dose; tocilizumab for grade ≥2. ICANS uncommon. Continuous B-cell depletion → hypogammaglobulinemia and serious infections: IVIG if recurrent, PJP + antiviral prophylaxis, vaccinate beforehand

R²: VTE — aspirin 81 mg if no other risk, LMWH/DOAC if high risk; rash (often grade 1–2; antihistamine, hold/reduce), neutropenia (50% grade 3–4 in AUGMENT), tumor flare, diarrhea. Dose by renal function
CAR-T: CRS and ICANS (REMS removed June 2025: stay near the center and no driving for 2 weeks), prolonged cytopenias, hypogammaglobulinemia; T-cell malignancy boxed warning
Zanubrutinib: bleeding (hold 3–7 days peri-procedure), AF, hypertension, neutropenia

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: BR > R-CHOP for PFS; no OS difference
24 Gy beats 4 Gy for local control
R² vs R at relapse: PFS HR 0.46
